missing_information_behavior: Do not recommend calcium until total dietary intake, life stage and existing products are assessed.
safety_exclusions: Do not equate low dairy intake with calcium deficiency.
Do not duplicate calcium from multivitamins or other products.
Do not advise indiscriminate high-dose calcium supplementation.
professional_escalation_conditions: Kidney stones, hypercalcemia, kidney disease, parathyroid disease, malabsorption or osteoporosis treatment.
population_and_context: People reporting little dairy intake; total calcium may still be adequate from fortified foods and non-dairy sources.
dose_constraints: No dose from this rule. Estimate total dietary calcium first; any supplement should bridge only a verified gap and account for elemental calcium.
certainty_and_limitations: NIH ODS Calcium fact sheet lists dietary sources, reference intakes and upper limits. Dairy intake alone is not a proxy for total calcium. This justification remains draft pending source passage verification, critical appraisal, certainty assessment and professional review.
